newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Rockets from Lebanon fired at Israel -sources.
newsitem.headline: Rockets from Lebanon fired at Israel -sources.

text.p: Guerrillas in Lebanon fired Katyusha rockets at northern Israel early on Tuesday but there were no immediate reports of injuries or damage, Israeli security sources said.
The attack just after 7 a.m. (0400 GMT) on Israel's northern Galilee came a day after violence in Lebanon claimed the lives of at least nine civilians.

Hizbollah, the Iranian-backed "Party of God," has been trying to oust Israeli troops and militiamen of the Israeli-backed South Lebanon Army from a 15-km (nine-mile) deep border zone set up inside Lebanon with the declared aim of preventing guerrilla attacks on Israel's northern border.

Israel distanced itself from the fighting on Monday. Lebanese militiamen led by pro-Israeli commander Antoine Lahd killed six civilians and wounded 36, many seriously, in shelling of the coastal town of Sidon.

Israel strongly denied firing the shells and blamed the incident on forces serving under Lahd around the Jezzine area outside the occupation zone patrolled by Israel and Lahd's South Lebanon Army (SLA).
Israeli military officials said Lahd's men were apparently avenging the deaths of three youths killed by a roadside bomb in the Jezzine area earlier on Monday.
